Convert an organization panel to the canonical npcompete schema

Source: R/archive.R
npc_standardize.Rd

Maps the columns of a source panel onto the organization-year schema that the archive and npc_build_metrics() use, so that every data source ends up in the same layout.

Usage

npc_standardize(df, source = c("soi_panel", "nccs_core"), bmf = NULL)

Arguments

df

A data frame from the source panel.

source

Which source layout df follows: "soi_panel", the NCCS SOI panel sample frame of Form 990 and 990-EZ filers, or "nccs_core", rows of the NCCS CORE 990combined files (see npc_build_nccs()).

bmf

For source = "nccs_core": the unified geocoded BMF, with at least EIN2, geo_county, geo_state_abbr, nteev2 and ruling_date. It supplies county, NTEEV2 and ruling year.

Value

A data frame with one row per organization-year and columns:

EIN2

Employer identification number (EIN-XX-XXXXXXX)

YEAR

Tax year

COUNTY_FIPS

Five-digit county FIPS code

CBSA_FIPS_GEOCODE

CBSA assigned when the address was geocoded; npc_get_orgs() adds CBSA_FIPS from the county crosswalk

NTEEV2

NTEE code in NCCS version 2 format

SUBSECTION

501(c) subsection

FILER_TYPE

"990", "990EZ", or NA for imputed gap years

EFILE

"EFILE", "PAPER" or NA

RULING_YEAR

Year the IRS granted exemption

REVOKED

TRUE in the year the exemption was revoked

REVOCATION_YEAR, REINSTATEMENT_YEAR

Years of automatic revocation and reinstatement, if any

TOTREV, TOTEXP, NETASS, TOTASS, TOTLIA

Revenue, expenses, net assets, assets and liabilities

REVPROG, REVCONT, REVINVE, FNDFEE

Program revenue, contributions, investment income and professional fundraising fees

FISYEAR, FISMO

Fiscal year and month the tax period ended

IMPUTED

TRUE for rows that fill a gap between filings; they have no financial data

SOURCE

The source file the row came from

Details

Both layouts are reduced to one row per EIN and tax year. The SOI panel repeats about 0.3% of EIN-years, mostly short-period returns after an accounting-period change; the row kept is a real filing over an imputed gap row, then the one from the latest source file (SOURCE), then the latest period end. This is the filing the NCCS CORE files keep.

For "nccs_core", the tax year is the year the fiscal period began (a December year end in Y is tax year Y, any other year end is Y - 1), matching the SOI panel. The CORE files for 2010 and 2011 come from NCCS's legacy pipeline: they record no form type, so FILER_TYPE is inferred from the 990-EZ limits (revenue under $200,000 and assets under $500,000; right for 89% of 2012-2013 returns), and they hold fewer returns than later years. Duplicate filings for an EIN and tax year are reduced to one: the latest extract, then the latest period end. For 990-EZ filers NETASS is total assets less total liabilities, as in the SOI panel, since the reported Part I figure often disagrees. CORE files have no fundraising fee or revocation fields, so FNDFEE, REVOKED, REVOCATION_YEAR and REINSTATEMENT_YEAR are NA, and CBSA_FIPS_GEOCODE is NA (CBSAs come from the county crosswalk).

Examples

raw <- data.frame(
  EIN2 = "EIN-01-0000001", TAXYEAR = 2019, COUNTY_FIPS = 1001,
  CENSUS_CBSA_FIPS = 33860, NTEEV2 = "ART-A20-RG", V501C = 3,
  SOURCE = "SOI_2020_PC", EFILE_X = "EFILE", ORG_RULING_YEAR = 1990,
  REVOKED_YEAR_X = 0, revocation_date = "", exemption_reinstatement_date = "",
  TOTREV = 1000, TOTEXP = 900, NETASS = 50, TOTASS = 80, TOTLIA = 30,
  REVPROG = 100, REVCONT = 800, REVINVE = 10, FNDFEE = NA, FISYEAR = 2019,
  FISMO = 12, MISSING_YEAR = 0 )
npc_standardize( raw )
#>             EIN2 YEAR COUNTY_FIPS CBSA_FIPS_GEOCODE     NTEEV2 SUBSECTION
#> 1 EIN-01-0000001 2019       01001             33860 ART-A20-RG          3
#>   FILER_TYPE EFILE RULING_YEAR REVOKED REVOCATION_YEAR REINSTATEMENT_YEAR
#> 1        990 EFILE        1990   FALSE              NA                 NA
#>   TOTREV TOTEXP NETASS TOTASS TOTLIA REVPROG REVCONT REVINVE FNDFEE FISYEAR
#> 1   1000    900     50     80     30     100     800      10     NA    2019
#>   FISMO IMPUTED      SOURCE
#> 1    12   FALSE SOI_2020_PC
